question: The rapid growth of AI technologies has led to the widespread use of deepfake video clips, making it almost impossible for most people to tell the difference between genuine and fake video content. This trend represents a serious threat to the integrity of the upcoming European elections because the spread of disinformation through deepfake video clips can undermine the democratic process.
In light of these developments I wish to ask the Commission about the EU’s comprehensive strategy for tackling the spread of disinformation through deepfake video clips. 1.
Could the Commission provide detailed information on the EU’s strategy for tackling the spread of disinformation through deepfake video clips?
Will the EU’s strategy be finalised and ready to implement in the little time that remains before the European elections?

How does the Commission intend to counteract AI-powered disinformation in an efficient way, especially when it is being driven by state actors and organisations whose aim it is to destabilise the EU, bearing in mind the scale and sophistication of these threats?
answer: The EU has scaled up its efforts to protect electoral integrity and address the misuse of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI); the strategy is already rolled-out and producing effects. With the Defence of Democracy Package (1), the Commission issued a recommendation on inclusive and resilient elections.

On that basis, most EU political parties signed a code of conduct (2) committing, among others, to abstain from using deepfakes. The AI Act (3) requires clear labelling of deepfakes and technical solutions such as watermarks that enable the marking and deception of AI generated content. The Commission encourages early implementation through the AI Pact (4).

The mitigation measures that Very Large Online Platforms and Search Engines (VLOPSEs) (5) need to employ under the Digital Services Act (DSA) (6) to counter disinformation apply also to AI generated content.

To ensure effective compliance, the Commission published guidelines (7) under the DSA on recommended measures for VLOPSEs to mitigate systemic risks that may impact electoral processes, including from generative AI. The guidelines build on the commitments of the 2022 Code of Practice on Disinformation (8).

The guidelines encourage early implementation of the regulation on the transparency and targeting of political advertisin g (9), which will require information of the AI Systems used to target and deliver such advertising. On 24 April 2024, the Commission tested election readiness of VLOPSEs, including in relation to information manipulation enabled by deep fakes.
The participants tested their procedures for the upcoming elections, to identify the specific areas that need improvement or where they could better coordinate.
Through its fact-checking network, including the EU elections Task Force (10), the European Digital Media Observatory detects and debunks disinformation across Europe, including deepfakes.
